citation: Primary (abstract opened): Demerouti, E., Bakker, A. B., Vardakou, I., & Kantas, A. (2003). The convergent validity of two burnout instruments: A multitrait-multimethod analysis. European Journal of Psychological Assessment, 19(1), 12-23. https://doi.org/10.1027//1015-5759.19.1.12. Also abstract-only: Demerouti, E., Mostert, K., & Bakker, A. (2010). Burnout and work engagement: A thorough investigation of the independency of both constructs. Journal of Occupational Health Psychology, 15(3), 209-222. https://doi.org/10.1037/a0019408. Full text opened (secondary): Campos, J.A.D.B., Carlotto, M.S., & Maroco, J. (2012). Oldenburg Burnout Inventory - Student Version: cultural adaptation and validation into Portuguese. Psicologia: Reflexao e Critica, 25(4), 709-718. http://www.redalyc.org/articulo.oa?id=18825219010. Original instrument: Demerouti & Nachreiner (1998), Demerouti et al. (2001) [not opened].
source_tier: Peer-reviewed (all three). The two primary papers are journal articles; the full text actually read is a peer-reviewed secondary validation study.
access_status: Demerouti 2003: abstract only (via university repository record). Demerouti 2010: abstract/summary only; full text behind login/paywall. Campos 2012: fully read (open access PDF). Demerouti & Nachreiner 1998 and Demerouti et al. 2001 original development papers: not opened. [uncertain] whether a full primary paper has been read: it has not.
sponsor_and_incentive: No funding stated on the repository pages for the 2003 paper [uncertain: not checked in full text]. OLBI is a free-to-use academic instrument; no known commercial incentive, unlike the MBI which is sold commercially by Mind Garden [uncertain: from background knowledge, not checked in an opened source].

Campos 2012, introduction: "Half of the items were formulated positively and half were formulated negatively."

date_and_recency: Instrument: Demerouti & Nachreiner 1998 (German), Demerouti et al. 2001 (English). Validation papers: 2003, 2010. Student adaptation 2012. Data collection windows not captured.
key_claims: OLBI is a self-report burnout measure with two dimensions, exhaustion and disengagement from work (called detachment/cynicism-like in comparisons with MBI). It was built on the premise that burnout is two-dimensional and can occur regardless of occupation. Exhaustion is meant to cover affective, physical and cognitive strain, not only emotional. Items are balanced positive/negative to avoid the MBI's wording confound. Demerouti 2003: factor structure supported and convergent/discriminant validity with the MBI-GS supported in a multitrait-multimethod design. Demerouti 2010 (abstract): across 528 workers, cynicism/dedication behaved as opposite ends of one attitude dimension, but exhaustion/vigor did not behave as opposite ends of one energy dimension, although highly correlated.
headline_figures: Demerouti 2003: n=232 Greek employees (banking, insurance, chemicals, per search summary). Demerouti 2010: n=528 South African construction employees. OLBI: 16 items, 4-point agreement scale (1 totally disagree to 4 totally agree), half positive and half negative (Campos 2012). Prior fit indices reported in Campos 2012 for OLBI factor model: chi2/df=1.90, GFI=.94, NFI=.90, CFI=.95, RMSEA=.062. Student version: n=958 Brazilian and 602 Portuguese students; two items dropped for low loadings (lambda<.50); Brazil exhaustion mean 2.70 (SD .48), Portugal 2.47 (SD .37); disengagement alpha=.700; correlation between OLBI-S exhaustion and disengagement .258.
sample_unit_and_population: Individual employees (2003: Greek, mixed occupations; 2010: South African construction workers) and university students (2012). No software-engineer sample in any opened source. Unit is the person, answering a questionnaire.
observed_vs_stated: Entirely self-reported questionnaire attitudes and feelings. No behavioural or physiological measures.
what_it_measures_or_defines: Two dimensions. Exhaustion: fatigue/strain after work demands, intended to span affective, physical and cognitive aspects. Disengagement: distancing oneself from work, its object, content and conditions, and negative attitudes toward it. Scored as agreement with 16 items (8 per dimension per Campos description of 'half'; per-dimension split of 8/8 is [uncertain], student version had 7 each before item removal). Reflects how the person feels and relates to work, not any observable artefact of their output.
mechanism_or_cause: In the opened sources, the OLBI is a measure, not a causal model. The wider Job Demands-Resources tradition by the same authors links high demands and scarce resources to exhaustion and disengagement [uncertain: not found in an opened source]. The 2010 abstract reports work pressure and autonomy as predictors and organisational commitment and mental health as outcomes, with a pattern consistent with the factor findings.
interventions_and_effects: None tested or recommended in the opened sources. It is a measurement instrument.
transfer_to_software_teams: Evidence base is general workforce, construction, and students. Authors' stance is that the two-dimension model applies regardless of occupation, but no software-engineer validation was seen in opened sources. For a repository proxy, the relevant point is that the OLBI itself is self-report, so any commit-based proxy would be a behavioural stand-in for a different kind of quantity.
limitations_stated: Campos 2012 (student version): limited convergent validity and internal consistency, acceptable composite reliability, no invariance between Brazil and Portugal; 'absence of cross-cultural validity'; one exhaustion item (O5) was a weak indicator in students. Original-paper limitations not read. Campos notes the OLBI factor structure has been reported with some problems of cross-sample factor weights.
counter_evidence: Demerouti 2010 (abstract): energy dimension (exhaustion vs vigor) was not supported as a single bipolar continuum, so the exhaustion/disengagement framing is not uncontested in relation to engagement. A UWO thesis (from search snippet only, not opened) reports failing to replicate Demerouti 2010 findings [uncertain]. Student version showed weak exhaustion-disengagement correlation (.258) and low convergent validity.
verification_status: Existence, citation details, sample sizes and headline validity conclusions of Demerouti 2003 and 2010: checked against abstract/repository pages only, not full text [uncertain]. Description of OLBI structure (16 items, 4-point scale, two dimensions, balanced wording): checked in an opened full text, but that text is a secondary source (Campos 2012), not the original paper [uncertain]. Item wording and the exact per-dimension content: not verified [uncertain]. Statement that a repository proxy cannot capture the construct is my inference, not a source claim.
usable_claim: The Oldenburg Burnout Inventory is a 16-item self-report questionnaire that treats burnout as two dimensions, exhaustion and disengagement from work, and was validated against the Maslach Burnout Inventory-General Survey in a 232-person Greek sample (Demerouti et al. 2003, abstract). It measures what people report feeling, so a measure built from repository activity can at most sit alongside it as a behavioural signal, not stand in for it. The second half is the essay's own inference, not the source's.
do_not_use: Do not claim the OLBI has been validated on software engineers. Do not cite per-item content, reliability coefficients or the 8/8 item split for the original instrument without opening Demerouti et al. 2001 or 2003 in full. Do not quote the Campos student-version figures (alpha, means, invariance results) as properties of the adult OLBI. Do not say BurnRiSc approximates or correlates with the OLBI; no opened source shows that.
overlap_with_existing_essays: Not checked against the three named essays [uncertain]; no grep of src/content/essays was performed.
